method: Used literal satisfiability probes: constructed architectures that satisfy the written TO/EC sentences while violating the product property the extraction is meant to preserve.

Reconciled findingDispositions against every D9/R-1 review and blind-axes JSON in artifacts, checking concrete finding objects/fields, raw identifier occurrence, uniqueness, and temporal supersession.
Audited the six non-STILL-OPEN rows against later reviews rather than treating a non-open label as evidence of closure.
Traced the proposed VERSIONING ownership through both artifacts and the register to test dependency direction and cycles.
Compared register bindingArtifact, claim notes, and architecture/07/09/11 after the v2 rebind. This differs from A1's primary missing-invariant inventory.
whatCouldHaveFailed: The 89-row table could have counted rows accurately while omitting real findings or inventing aggregate labels.
A finding marked addressed could have been reopened by a later review also present in the same table.
A total-but-unnamed remedy partition could permit materially different CI actions to collapse.
A falsifiedBy sentence could merely negate its invariant or fail to describe a behavior that actually violates it.
The R-1 boundary could name four components without assigning effectful execution, publication, cancellation, or telemetry responsibility.
The register could bind an unaccepted artifact while prose continued to say no binding exists.
positiveAssessment: The consequence-based altitude test is a real repair. Schema form no longer decides architectural status, and the exit-class example correctly focuses on external custody and irreversible compatibility cost.
DEFAULT STILL-OPEN is the right failure posture for a disposition system; demoting a contract must never discharge findings implicitly.
EC-7 is more honest about adapter/provider TCB authority than v1, and EC-8 at least restores that a boundary must exist.
Stopping further wire-only D9/R-1 version churn remains correct.

sourceReconciliation.subjectClaim: 89 findings were raised; 83 are STILL-OPEN and 6 accounted
sourceReconciliation.conservativeConclusion: At least 17 concrete finding IDs are absent and at least four rows use labels not present in the historical D9/R-1 review corpus. Therefore 89 is only the table row count, not the finding population. This conclusion does not depend on classifying every heterogeneous legacy key.

literalBadModels.allowedByText: The host derives one operational-failed termination and writes process exit 4, while a serializer bug emits success/0 in the machine envelope. TO-1..11 require one derivation and distinct rendering but never require envelope/process parity.
literalBadModels.violatedArchitectureProperty: A successfully emitted finite-command envelope and process outcome must agree.

literalBadModels.allowedByText: An unsupported baseline recipe terminates indeterminate but still emits mass comparison-derived findings. It is not a green outcome, so TO-5/10 do not prohibit the damaging effect.
literalBadModels.violatedArchitectureProperty: Unsupported comparison must perform no comparison and emit no derived findings.

literalBadModels.allowedByText: A missing identity is reported as expired without tombstone evidence. No TO invariant constrains the expiry/never-existed distinction.
literalBadModels.violatedArchitectureProperty: Expiry is claimable only with retained tombstone evidence.

literalBadModels.allowedByText: A project-resolution or option-parse failure exits before HostTermination construction and emits untyped stderr. TO-1 is scoped to command kinds and does not define the pre-admission boundary or FailureResult constructibility.
literalBadModels.violatedArchitectureProperty: Stable machine failure must be constructible before project or Run admission.

literalBadModels.allowedByText: Cold and resident hosts return identical Run bodies, but the resident provider leaks a child process and observes different cancellation/telemetry semantics. No surface flag branches on lifetime, process supervision is nominally outside the core, and EC-3 compares only Runs.
literalBadModels.violatedArchitectureProperty: Lifetime neutrality includes semantic re-entrancy, cancellation, cleanup, and progress behavior across the declared execution boundary.

findings.title: The 89-finding anti-laundering table is not a complete inventory of the source reviews
evidence: the table has 89 unique rows, so its local arithmetic is correct
source reconciliation finds 17 concrete omitted findings: A1-on-A3-D9-1..6, A3-D9-1..6, and B-D9V15-01..05
four table labels do not occur in the historical D9/R-1 review corpus: A1-D9-V15, A1-R1, A1-R1V13, B-R1
all five omitted B-D9V15 findings are confirmed open by artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.5.review-a1-confirm.json
findings.impact: The mechanism introduced to prevent finding laundering launders findings through an invalid denominator. 'DEFAULT STILL-OPEN' protects only rows that made it into the table.
findings.requiredChange: Generate a deterministic inventory with one source artifact and JSON path per finding, distinguish finding IDs from aggregate/review labels, and have an independent checker compare the source set to dispositions. Do not publish a total until the denominator is independently validated.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that the 17 omitted objects were explicitly excluded by a declared, reviewed population rule rather than overlooked.

findings.title: The table counts six findings as accounted even when later retained reviews reopen or only partially repair them
evidence: A1-D9-V14-01 is ADDRESSED-IN-DEMOTED-ARTIFACT, while table row A1-D9-V15C-01 remains STILL-OPEN and its source explicitly revises V14-01 from CLOSED to PARTIAL because D10 is optional
A2-D9-V12-05 is called detailed and addressed, yet tombstone-backed expiry is missing from the architectural invariants and has public remedy semantics
A2-R1-06 and A2-R1-V11-02 are counted promoted even though EC-8 leaves provider/effect placement incomplete and EC-7 remains limited by ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT
the table has no supersedes/reopens relation or PARTIAL disposition, so contradictory rows coexist
findings.impact: Counting every non-STILL-OPEN row as accounted reintroduces Error 5: a claim can be closed in one row and open in a later row, with the summary selecting the stronger status.
findings.requiredChange: Add temporal precedence and explicit PARTIAL/REOPENED states. A later finding that revises an earlier disposition must mechanically downgrade it. Recompute accounted only after architectural versus detailed classification and independent adjudication.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A rule showing 'accounted' means only 'mentioned' and is never interpreted as addressed; the row evidence and log use it as repair credit.

findings.title: TO-1..11 still permit false machine claims and destructive comparison behavior
evidence: TO-9 does not name or define the six non-collapsible remedy classes, so totality can be satisfied by a coarser partition
BM-D9-PARITY satisfies the written set while envelope and process disagree
BM-D9-BASELINE permits mass net-new findings under an indeterminate termination
BM-D9-IDENTITY permits an unsupported expiry claim
BM-D9-PREADMIT leaves the most failure-prone path outside the machine envelope
orphan-publication recovery and exit-zero-not-attestation also remain absent
findings.impact: The extraction cannot replace D9 architecture: implementations with materially wrong CI action, evidence claims, and baseline effects still conform literally.
findings.requiredChange: Bind the named six-class semantic partition and add invariants for envelope parity, pre-admission typed failure, orphan recovery, tombstone-backed expiry, baseline no-comparison/no-derived-findings, and exit 0 not being attestation. Give each a concrete counterexample and handoff test.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A referenced binding claim that already owns each omitted property and is listed as a D9 dependency.

findings.title: falsifiedBy strings are not yet a counterexample or production-handoff contract
evidence: the strings have no stable IDs, scenario inputs, expected refusal/observation, ownership, or trace into future acceptance tests
many merely negate the invariant rather than instantiate a competing plausible design
EC-5 says a design promising both contenders complete falsifies integrity-not-liveness, but a serializable implementation may legitimately complete both; that promise is not itself a violation
EC-4 treats a deployment-specific argument as a behavioral falsifier even if the underlying storage protocol is actually safe
v2 has no detailedDesignHandoff section despite resolves claiming B-SC-10 ACCEPTED
findings.impact: A future detailed contract can green-check its own schema while never exercising these prose negatives. Some listed negatives would also reject valid stronger implementations.
findings.requiredChange: Replace each prose negation with an identified scenario and expected architectural response; correct EC-4/5; require every future production contract to trace each case to independent executable acceptance evidence or a reviewed impossibility argument.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A mandatory external handoff rule that already imports these exact strings with independently specified expected behavior.

findings.title: EC-1 and EC-8 still allow lifetime-dependent effects because the four-way boundary is named but not allocated
evidence: EC-1 tests only parameters, fields, or environment reads that branch on lifetime; hidden global/provider state or lifetime-dependent cleanup needs none of those forms
BM-R1-EFFECTS preserves Run-body parity while cancellation, child cleanup, and telemetry semantics differ

EC-8 places admission, grants, resolution, and process supervision outside but does not allocate provider execution, fact/rule/policy evaluation, budget accounting, storage publication, cancellation, or telemetry
EC-3 does not state identical Snapshot, Plan, toolchain, environment, and exact Coverage preconditions
findings.impact: The extraction cannot determine what must be lifetime-neutral or whether a proposed provider/publication design conforms. A surface-neutral core can remain semantically lifetime-dependent.
findings.requiredChange: Define semantic re-entrancy and exact parity preconditions; provide an inside/outside responsibility table for core, host, providers, and storage; place effectful execution, publication, cancellation, and telemetry; then derive conformance cases from that boundary.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A separately binding boundary artifact covering these responsibilities and referenced by EC-1/8.

findings.title: TO-8 claims VERSIONING ownership but neither artifact nor register establishes a coherent one-way dependency
evidence: v2 says D9 explicitly depends on VERSIONING for additive-only exit evolution
the register leaves D9.dependsOn empty
versioning-policy.v1 decisionDependencies includes D9 and still cites d9-exit-contract.v1.4
making the v2 prose dependency real without changing VERSIONING creates a D9↔VERSIONING cycle
findings.impact: B-SC-05 is not closed. D9 can appear independently closable while importing candidate policy, or both claims can become mutually blocked with stale authority.
findings.requiredChange: Choose one-way ownership. A coherent option is for D9 to define and custody-tag the exact class semantics, while VERSIONING owns generic evolution policy and treats D9 as an application rather than a decision dependency. Whatever is chosen must be identical in both artifacts and the register.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A documented non-circular distinction between articulation and truth dependency reflected in the authoritative register.

findings.title: D9 and R-1 were rebound to v2 before acceptance while prose and even the R-1 register note still say no binding exists
evidence: v2 declares CANDIDATE-UNREVIEWED but D9, R-1, and METHOD.ALTITUDE were immediately rebound to the whole artifact
architecture/07 and architecture/09 say D9 has no accepted binding
R-1's register note says there is currently no accepted binding artifact next to bindingArtifact=v2
architecture/11 describes scope-correction-a3.v2 as 'Rejected candidate; require v2', a filename-only repair that is semantically impossible
architecture/10 still presented v1's withdrawn percentages and form-based field/schema rule while the register bound v2's consequence-based altitudeTest
check-claims reports clean because it cannot evaluate semantic aliases or note/binding contradictions
findings.impact: The v1 premature-rebind error recurred on v2. Different readers again receive mutually exclusive authority answers from checker-clean documents.
findings.requiredChange: Leave D9 and R-1 bindingArtifact null until an independently accepted architecture object exists; record v2 as incompleteCandidateArtifact. METHOD.ALTITUDE may point specifically at v2#altitudeTest because that portion survived review. Repair 07/09/11/register atomically.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A defined register semantics under which bindingArtifact means 'latest rejected draft' rather than authority; current prose uses accepted-binding semantics.

findings.title: The v2 resolves map says B-SC-04 and B-SC-10 are accepted as repaired when the object does not implement their required changes
evidence: resolves.B-SC-04 says missing invariants were restored as TO-9..11, but the independently enumerated omitted set remains larger
resolves.B-SC-10 says every invariant now has a falsifying counterexample, but falsifiedBy prose lacks concrete cases and no design handoff exists
resolves.B-SC-09 says binding was updated atomically while architecture/07/09/11 and the R-1 note contradict the rebind
findings.impact: A local syntactic addition is promoted into global closure, exactly the recurring error pattern this exercise records.
findings.requiredChange: Use PARTIAL/OPEN dispositions tied to each required-change clause, not ACCEPTED based on field presence. A resolve closes only after an independent review finds the original falsifier no longer constructible.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A narrower documented meaning of ACCEPTED that explicitly does not imply the finding's required change is satisfied; that would make the resolves map misleading by design.

resolves.B-SCV2-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: finding denominator is false; at least 17 concrete findings are omitted.
resolves.B-SCV2-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: accounted count includes contradicted or partial dispositions.
resolves.B-SCV2-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: D9 literal bad models remain conforming.
resolves.B-SCV2-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: counterexamples and mandatory design handoff are incomplete.
resolves.B-SCV2-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: R-1 semantic parity and responsibility allocation remain incomplete.
resolves.B-SCV2-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: D9/VERSIONING ownership is inconsistent and potentially cyclic.
resolves.B-SCV2-07: PRESENTATION-FIX-APPLIED: D9/R-1 unbound again and v2 recorded as incomplete; substantive replacement remains open.
resolves.B-SCV2-08: OPEN-BLOCKER: v2 resolve language overstates partial repairs.

sealedPropertiesCovered: architecture/10 method rule 4 — artifact back-references must preserve the decision they claim to encode
architecture/10 method rule 7 — an unreviewed claim is not a settled premise
ARCH.RUN-MULTIAXIS — verdict, Coverage, lifecycle, and durability remain distinct
ARCH.CONFINEMENT-HONESTY — interfaces and dependency lists do not establish capability absence
knownLimitations: The heterogeneous historical reviews do not share one finding schema. This review does not assert the final true denominator; it conservatively proves v2's denominator false from 17 omitted concrete finding objects/fields and four unsupported table labels.
This review does not author scope-correction v3, the missing D9 architecture, or the complete R-1 boundary.

No shipping implementation source was inspected because v2 makes greenfield architecture and review-history claims; the load-bearing 89/accounted assertions were checked directly against their source review artifacts.
The literal bad models establish underconstraint, not that an implementation would intentionally choose those designs.
confidence: high on source-set, temporal-disposition, literal-underconstraint, dependency, and authority findings; medium-high on the final allocation of D9 versus VERSIONING ownership
sealRecommendation: Accept the consequence-based altitude test and default-open principle as progress. Do not bind D9 or R-1 to v2, do not count the 89/83/6 summary as authoritative, and do not seal METHOD.ALTITUDE until the coordinator separates the accepted altitude fragment from the rejected extractions.
